text:
michelle (PM): Quick sync — we need to reconcile routing economics asks from sales and launch criteria for multi-region tenant isolation. TL;DR: customers repeatedly asking for predictable p95 latency + EU data residency guarantees. I sketched a phased plan; want quick reactions.

sam (eng): +1 on phased. we can offer 3 tiers: shared, reserved, isolated. main risk is telemetry surface to enforce p95 contracts.

diego (infra): agree. capacity-wise reserved pools are straightforward. isolated (tenant-dedicated) is expensive — need commit sizes. can we soften with soft-eviction?

ara (architect): preference: start with policy-driven routing + canary. ship routing templates first (region + residency predicates) before full tenant isolation plumbing. keeps rollout small.

raj (sales): customers want SLA language. They won't sign unless we commit to regional binding and a fallback behavior. also ask: what are upgrade paths from shared->reserved->isolated?

olivia (customer-success): adding: several pilot customers asked for audit logs + KMS integration for isolated lanes. that's a must for Q4 pilots.

michelle (PM): proposed launch criteria (draft):
- Pilot customers: 2 enterprise pilot customers with residency needs
- Perf: p95 < 250ms for reserved lane on standard prompt mix
- Ops: auto-eviction playbook + rollback within 5m
- Security: at-rest KMS + audit streaming enabled

sam (eng): realistic? p95 250ms depends on model and seq len. need model-aware routing to hit that. suggest: p95 by route+model profile (e.g., 0-512 tokens).

ara (architect): add routing policy example for discussion:
```yaml
routing_policy:
  - name: eu_residency
    match: request.customer.residency == "EU"
    prefer: region: eu-west-1
    fallback: region: global
  - name: latency_guard
    match: request.latency_estimate > 200ms
    action: route_to: lower_cost_model_variant
```

diego (infra): ops note: fallback to global needs capacity headroom; otherwise fallback will just increase SLO violations. we should gate fallback on a capacity threshold check.

raj (sales): can we make the fallback behavior configurable per-customer? some customers prefer strict failover (reject) vs degrade (lower quality model).

michelle (PM): yes — per-tenant policy overrides in roadmap. priority: policy templates first, then per-tenant overrides, then dedicated tenancy. timeline suggestion:
- Q1: routing templates + telemetry (templates + metrics)
- Q2: per-tenant overrides + canary deploy tooling
- Q3: reserved pools + legal SLA draft
- Q4: isolated lanes + KMS + audit integration (pilot)

olivia (customer-success): this lines up with pilot asks. please add an explicit acceptance test for audit log completeness (no gaps > 1m).

sam (eng): dev tasks I see: metrics schema, routing engine supports predicate DSL, per-tenant config store, canary traffic shaper. estimate: 8 Sprints across eng teams if parallelized.

ara (architect): open question: how do we verify economic impact? need a simulation harness to run traffic mixes and show cost delta shared->reserved->isolated. I can prototype a small tool.

michelle (PM): action items:
- ara: prototype simulation harness + share by next Wed
- sam: draft metrics schema + p95 calc and post to /docs/link
- diego: capacity gating proposal + soft-eviction playbook
- raj/olivia: surface pilot customers + required legal asks

launch-bot: Created ticket PROD-2981: "Routing templates + residency pilot runway" and assigned to michelle.

raj (sales): thanks — i'll loop in legal for draft SLA language.

michelle (PM): ok — if we agree, i'll turn this thread into a short PRD and schedule a 30m sync later this week. any blocking concerns?

sam (eng): none from eng that stop us starting templates. small ask: include example prompt mixes we should use for perf tests.

olivia (customer-success): i'll send two pilot customer contacts and their minimal compliance checklist.

michelle (PM): perfect. will collect notes and post PRD link here. thanks everyone :rocket:
